candidates.designation: 'candidate companion' / 'LHS 3844 c' (Nagel et al. 2026, Sect. 4.3.2, Fig. A.6, Table B.5); exoplanet.eu 'LHS 3844 c' (Candidate)
candidates.tier_reason: Tentative RV signal in archival ESPRESSO data only: periodogram FAP 2.1% (not significant), although a two-planet model is favoured by Delta lnZ = 10.97. Nagel et al. note it sits near the second-order daily alias of b (~6.24 d); Hacker et al. place that alias at 6.47 +/- 0.30 d and call their model comparison inconclusive. The two papers use the same 25 ESPRESSO RVs, so they are not independent, and their periods disagree (6.8758 vs 6.694 d). Neither claims a planet.
candidates.orbit_flags: RV-only, non-transiting (no BLS peak in TESS near 6.88 d). Period, K and Msini from the Nagel et al. 2026 two-planet fit (CRIRES+ + ESPRESSO, circular). Cross-check: Hacker et al. 2026 Sect. 6.5 recover P2 = 6.694 +/- 0.007 d, K2 = 3.0 +/- 0.4 m/s, M2 sin i = 2.5 +/- 0.4 Mearth from the same ESPRESSO data. No semi-major axis published; writer derives from P and M*. Eccentricity not fitted (fixed 0).
candidates.reference: Nagel et al. 2026, 'Mass determination of the ultra-short-period planet LHS 3844 b. First K-band radial velocity measurements with CRIRES+', arXiv:2603.28238, Sect. 4.3.2 and Table B.5; see also Hacker et al. 2026, A&A, arXiv:2603.28237, Sect. 6.5

S2.citation: Hacker et al. 2026, 'Weighing the mass of LHS 3844 b', arXiv:2603.28237 (A&A)
S2.what: independent fit P2 = 6.694 d, K2 = 3.0 m/s, M2 sin i = 2.5 Mearth; alias at 6.47 d; 'inconclusive'

candidates.designation: fourth body of the two-circumbinary-object model (Rattanamala et al. 2023, Table 8); exoplanet.eu 'RR Cae (AB)c' (Candidate)
candidates.tier_reason: Eclipse-timing (light-travel-time) inference from one O-C curve. The authors say it is 'hard to conclude that there are two circumbinary objects', since the two-object model differs from the one-planet one only through a single 1984 eclipse time. Pulley et al. 2025 report new 2022-2025 timings that none of the recent RR Cae models fit, and note a Lanza-type magnetic mechanism is energetically possible for exactly this second modulation. ETV planets around post-common-envelope binaries have a poor record.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.note: planets_confirmed.csv row 290 gives period 2.018 d and a = 0.01735 au, which belong to the REFUTED 2-d signal of Mahadevan et al. 2021 (OEC mislabels that signal 'GJ 1151 c' with P = 2.018 d), combined with mass 10.62 Mearth of the real planet. The confirmed planet has P = 389.7 d, Msini 10.62 Mearth (NASA pscomppars 'GJ 1151 c', Blanco-Pozo et al. 2023) and a = 0.57 au (Blanco-Pozo et al. 2023 abstract). Period and a need correcting.

Unconfirmed tab row 23 (TOI-7032.01, PC) duplicates confirmed-tab row 539 (GJ 523 b). Kroft et al. 2026 (arXiv:2603.24682, preprint, 'Draft version March 27, 2026') confirm it by NEID RVs: 23.5 +/- 3.3 Mearth, 2.55 Rearth, P = 17.75 d; exoplanet.eu lists it Confirmed. NASA pscomppars does NOT list it yet and the TOI table still says PC, so the confirmation rests on a preprint. GJ 523 = TOI-7032 = TIC 22903436 = HIP 66954 = BD+39 2675.

Systems tab shows 'WD 1856+534 b:4386 [>13 MJ - likely BD]'. 4386 Mearth is the Vanderburg et al. 2020 upper limit (13.8 MJup). Limbach et al. 2025 (arXiv:2504.16982, JWST MIRI thermal emission) constrain the mass to no more than ~6 MJup and 'rule out previously unexcluded low-mass brown dwarf scenarios'; NASA ps holds a Limbach 2025 row with 1652.7 Mearth. The 'likely BD' flag is out of date.

On the confirmed tab (Qian et al. 2012, P = 4350 d). NASA sets pl_controv_flag = 1. Pulley et al. 2025 (arXiv:2507.06748) find none of the recent RR Cae ETV models (Rattanamala et al. 2023, which move b to 15.0-16.6 yr) fit 2022-2025 timings. The writer may want a caveat.
